---
title: "Methodology"
subtitle: "How every number on this site is produced."
---

Everything here is generated by an internal, **command-only** harness (`harness/` in the repo) that
drives *real Whetstone* — the same five MCP tools the server ships. It never runs in CI; a maintainer
runs it and commits the artifacts under `harness/out/`, which this site only reads.

## The cold → capture → warm loop

This is the same three-stage loop the [Home](index.qmd#how-it-works) page walks through — there it's
introduced as "Cold, captured, then warm" for a first-time reader; here it's the harness running that
same loop mechanically, at scale, over every scenario.

For each scenario (a skill's prompt + an arbitrary subjective preference):

1. **Cold** — generate the output with an **empty** store. Record whether the preference was honored
   (usually not — the "before").
2. **Capture** — replay the scripted correction through Whetstone's `capture` tool, exactly as a user
   correcting the skill would. The preference becomes a tracked learning or issue, committed to the
   per-skill store.
3. **Warm** — `recall` the now-captured store, inject that learned layer, regenerate, and check again.
   Reinforce each learning (a repeated correction) so its weight/recurrence grows, and iterate until
   the preference is honored for a set streak of consecutive warm runs.

Generation is done by the live model via the Claude Agent SDK with the scenario's skill mounted.
A deterministic **stub** generator exercises the identical pipeline with no API calls, so the wiring
is verifiable without spend.

## What "honored" means

Each preference carries a deterministic **check** against the generated primary output — `table.py`
for great-tables, `index.html` for frontend-design, `plot.py` for plotnine, `deck.py` for pptx
(comment- and docstring-stripped so prose can't fool it): a substring, a regex, or their absence.
That check — not a subjective judgement — decides whether a run honored the preference.

## The two metrics

- **Runs-to-stick** counts **warm** runs only (the cold baseline never counts), so a lucky cold run
  can't claim credit before the correction existed.
- **Value-over-time** is the learning's `weight`/`recurrence` straight from the `recall` payload each
  run.

## Honesty

No metric is hand-set. A metric a scenario can't support honestly stays `null` with a note — the same
stance `whetstone metrics` takes for its labeled KPIs. The store runs on the
**sentence-transformers** backend (the calibrated one); when retrieval genuinely misses a seeded
entry, the site shows that miss rather than hiding it.

## The labeled KPIs — the calibration harness

Three §11 KPIs need a *labeled* ground truth that ordinary usage never has, so the runtime `metrics`
tool returns them as `null` by design: **capture-rate**, **regressions-prevented**, and
**retrieval-precision**. A second command-only harness, `python -m harness.calibrate`, computes them
against a small **hand-labeled set** ([`harness/calibration/labels.yaml`](https://github.com/HrudithL/whetstone/blob/main/harness/calibration/labels.yaml))
— a human vouches for every case — and writes `out/calibration.json`, which the
**[Metrics](metrics.qmd)** page reads:

- **retrieval-precision** — for each labeled `(intent → relevant scopes)` case, seed a store, `recall`,
  and score the returned scopes against the labels (precision / recall / F1). Key-free.
- **capture-rate** — for each labeled correction turn, drive `capture` and count how often it lands as
  `committed` / `reinforced` rather than a no-op. Key-free.
- **regressions-prevented** — a key-free **proxy** checks that an in-scope issue is recalled for an
  intent that would violate it (so the model is warned before it can regress); a live `--agent`
  cold-vs-warm generation is the published figure.

The same command also scores a fourth, **experimental** entry in `calibration.json` that is not one
of the §11 product KPIs: **`same_polarity_contradiction`** (§M7c) — precision/recall of the narrow
antonym/negation heuristic in `capture`'s dedup path (see [Tools](tools.qmd#capture)'s
`possible_contradiction` status), scored against its own labeled section in the same
`labels.yaml`. This one is not shown on the [Metrics](metrics.qmd) page — it measures a spike-status
heuristic, not a headline product number — but it is computed the same honest way: a small
hand-labeled set of contradiction pairs (should fire) and genuine-duplicate pairs (should not),
run through real `capture`.

The boundary is deliberate and stays intact: the **runtime `metrics` tool still returns `null`** for
these three — only this published showcase, linked to the labeled set and the runner that produced it,
shows the numbers. When `calibration.json` is absent the Metrics page falls back to the same
null-with-note it always showed.

## What was taught, and how "honored" is judged

Every preference below is an **arbitrary house-style choice** — the point is only that a correction,
once given, is tracked and re-applied, not that the choice is objectively right. The `check` column
is the exact deterministic test that decides whether a generated table honored the preference.

```{python}
# | echo: false
# | output: asis
import html
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from _showcase import scenarios_meta  # noqa: E402
from IPython.display import HTML, display  # noqa: E402

# An HTML table (not Markdown), so a check pattern containing regex metacharacters like `|` is shown
# EXACTLY — a Markdown pipe table would split the cell and corrupt the audited check.
def td(text: str) -> str:
    return f"<td>{html.escape(' '.join(str(text).split()))}</td>"


head = ("<tr><th>scenario</th><th>diff.</th><th>preference</th><th>polarity</th>"
        "<th>scope</th><th>rule</th><th>check</th></tr>")
body = []
# Every scenario across all skills, straight from the committed YAMLs — independent of whether the
# harness has actually been run for it yet. The Before/After and Metrics pages only show a scenario
# once `python -m harness.run --agent` has populated its `out/` artifacts, so a scenario can appear
# here (describing what it teaches and how compliance is checked) before it appears there. The
# `check` column is the exact test that will be run against that scenario's primary output
# (`table.py` for great-tables, `index.html` for frontend-design, `deck.py` for pptx).
for s in scenarios_meta():
    for p in s["preferences"]:
        chk = f"{html.escape(p['check']['kind'])} · <code>{html.escape(p['check']['pattern'])}</code>"
        body.append(
            f"<tr>{td(s['name'])}{td(s['difficulty'])}<td><code>{html.escape(p['id'])}</code></td>"
            f"{td(p['polarity'])}{td(p['scope'])}{td(p['body'])}<td>{chk}</td></tr>"
        )
# Wrap in a horizontally-scrollable container: this table is wide (the rule + check columns carry
# long text), so it scrolls within the content column instead of spilling past the "On this page" TOC.
display(HTML(
    "<div style='overflow-x:auto;max-width:100%'>"
    f"<table class='table'><thead>{head}</thead><tbody>{''.join(body)}</tbody></table></div>"
))
```

## Where every number comes from

The site reads only committed files under `harness/out/`; nothing is computed at page-render time
beyond formatting. Per scenario:

| file | feeds |
| --- | --- |
| `cold/<primary output>` | the **Before** panel (`table.{py,png,html}` / `index.html` / `deck.py`) |
| `warm/<primary output>` | the **After** panel (same set, generated with the learned layer) |
| `learned_layer.txt` | the middle **learned-layer** panel (verbatim injected prompt text) |
| `recall.json` | the structured recall payload behind the learned layer |
| `runs.jsonl` | per-run honored map + weight/recurrence — the raw record |
| `summary.json` | per-preference **runs-to-stick** + **value-over-time** + store usage KPIs |
| `../metrics.json` | the cross-scenario **aggregate** and the dashboard charts |

Each headline number traces to `summary.json` / `metrics.json`, which trace to `runs.jsonl`, which is
written straight from the tool calls.

and PowerPoint decks). The same substrate — attach, recall, capture, revise — applies unchanged to a
**code-improvement** skill (objective ground truth: tests, lint, types) and a **context-organizing**

## Reproduce it

```bash
pip install -e ".[showcase,embeddings]"
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...     # or harness/.env
python -m harness.run --agent            # regenerate out/ (paid, command-only)
python -m harness.calibrate              # labeled KPIs -> out/calibration.json (key-free)
python -m harness.metrics                # aggregate -> out/metrics.json (folds in calibration.json)
```
